_note: Each animal's body in battle (scripts/battle/battle_sim.gd, battle_army.gd, scripts/fx/unit_view.gd, model_stage.gd, battle_field.gd). size: how big it's drawn, its longest side in field tiles (a bird's wingspan, an upright animal's height), whatever its model's own proportions; a Mythic's is its hero size. footprint and width: its true body size on the ground, tiles (its length nose to tail, or wingtip to wingtip, and how wide it is). A strike is measured nose to nose: a melee animal hits when the gap between its body's end and its target's is within its reach, and stands at its slot that far from its target's body. A shot is measured body to body (the circles): a shooter's card range means what it did before bodies had footprints. The room it takes in the fight at all times (spacing in a line, being pushed apart, knockbacks, a body going down) is a circle between its width and its length (the square root of the two, across), so a line of bodies stands clear and nothing walks through one; the fight's radius is half of that. reach: how far its strike extends beyond its body, tiles (jaws, a paw, a horn, a trunk, tentacles): it hits from that far, stands that far from its target's body (its slot), and its lunge never carries its body past the target's footprint; a shooter's (shooter true: its card's or its class's range is over a tile) is that range, as before. Fliers' bodies run across their heading (wingtip to wingtip) and one flying over another is no overlap; a Burrow animal underground has no body on show. across: its long side runs across the way it faces, not nose to tail (an upright animal with its arms spread: the Orangutan, the Gorilla, the Yeti; a flier's wings always do): its body's room runs across too, and its reach is measured from its front, half its width out. pose_up: the tallest it stands on the screen in a fight (its real outline in its tallest pose of idle, walk, attack, fidget and victory, posed by its skeleton) as a share of how tall it stands (its outline in its idle pose, facing whichever way makes it tallest): a little over 1 for most, under 1 for a bird that perches tall and fights lower (measured from the models: ModelStage.tallest_share; tests/test_sizes.gd keeps it true). limits: how big animals may look on the screen, as a share of the screen's height: average_target_pct is what a typical animal should be in a normal fight (Clash Royale's are 5-7%), unit_max_pct the most any animal may be (the biggest Tanks) and hero_max_pct the most a Mythic hero may be; the camera never zooms in past them for any animal's tallest pose (battle_field.gd; it stops camera_margin_pct short, for the touch of squash and stretch and the lean on top), the feel report measures them (tests/feel_report.gd SIZE) and tests/test_sizes.gd fails if one is over. Elite Specialists are drawn feel.json army elite_scale bigger. limits: the share of the phone screen's height an animal stands (its outline in its idle pose): average_target_pct for a typical one, at most unit_max_pct (the biggest Tanks) and hero_max_pct (a Mythic hero) as the camera zooms in; its tallest poses (an attack rearing up, a celebration: pose_up) may rise to pose_allowance times that for a moment (one whose tallest pose would rise more counts as that much taller).
